items.quote: What you'll learn
items.text: The concept of arc length. The concept of measuring an arc. How to find the relation between chords of a circle and its arcs.

items.quote: Arc length is a part of a circle's circumference proportional with its measure
items.claim: Arc length is a part of a circle's circumference proportional with its measure.

items.quote: Where the arc length = The measure of the arc
items.claim: Arc length = (measure of the arc / measure of the circle) × circumference of the circle.
items.formula: $\text{arc length}=\dfrac{\text{measure of the arc}}{\text{measure of the circle}}\times \text{circumference of the circle}$

items.quote: M is a circle with radius length of 5 cm
items.stem: In the opposite figure: M is a circle with radius length of 5 cm, $m(\widehat{AB})=108^\circ$. Find the length of $\widehat{AB}$ ($\pi=3.14$).
solution: Arc length $=\dfrac{\text{Measure of the arc}}{\text{Measure of the circle}}\times$ circumference of the circle.

items.quote: In the same circle (or in congruent circles), if the measures of arcs
items.claim: Corollary (1): In the same circle (or in congruent circles), if the measures of arcs are equal, then the lengths of the arcs are equal, and conversely.

items.claim: Corollary (2): In the same circle (or in congruent circles), if the measures of arcs are equal, then their chords are equal in length, and conversely.

learning_objectives.label: Measure arcs from central angles
learning_objectives.description: Determine the measure of an arc as the measure of its central angle, and find the measures of adjacent arcs, semicircles and the circle by adding or subtracting.

learning_objectives.label: Calculate arc length
learning_objectives.description: Calculate the length of an arc as the fraction (measure of the arc / measure of the circle) of the circumference, and compare arcs of equal measure in different circles.

learning_objectives.label: Relate arcs, chords and parallels
learning_objectives.description: Use the corollaries on equal arcs, equal chords and parallel chords or tangents to prove arcs or chords are equal and to find unknown lengths.
